name: Tandoori Chicken
ingredients: 1 whole chicken (about 1.2 kg), skin removed, cut into pieces
1 cup thick plain yogurt (full-fat, hung for 2 hours to drain whey)
1 tablespoon Kashmiri red chili powder (for color, not heat)
1 teaspoon garam masala (clove, cardamom, cinnamon blend)
2 tablespoons mustard oil (or vegetable oil, for marination)
1 teaspoon black salt (kala namak) or regular salt
2 tablespoons chickpea flour (besan), dry roasted until aromatic
Optional: a pinch of red food coloring (traditional, but can omit)
Fresh cilantro and lemon wedges for garnish
instructions: 1. Pat chicken pieces dry and score deep slits (2-3 per piece) to allow marinade penetration.

2. In a bowl, whisk yogurt until smooth. Add ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, cumin, garam masala, lemon juice, mustard oil, salt, and besan. Mix into a smooth paste. (If using food coloring, add now.)
3. Coat chicken thoroughly with marinade, massaging into slits. Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours (or overnight for deeper flavor).
4. Remove chicken from fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Preheat tandoor (or oven) to 450°F (230°C). If using oven, place a baking tray lined with foil on the bottom rack to catch drips.

5. Thread chicken pieces onto skewers (if available) or place directly on a wire rack set over a baking sheet. For extra smoke, place a small bowl of hot coals or a piece of charcoal in the oven (optional).
6. Cook for 25-30 minutes, turning once halfway, until charred in spots and internal temp reaches 165°F (74°C). For chargrill effect, broil for last 2 minutes.
7. Rest for 5 minutes, then brush with melted butter or ghee. Garnish with cilantro and lemon wedges. Serve hot with naan and mint chutney.
description: A fiery, smoky embrace of yogurt-tenderized chicken, charred to perfection in the tandoor's ancient heat.
